archetype.name: Play-In Team (cold start)
archetype.definition: A Giannis-led roster coming off a 43-39 season whose talent and track record point to the middle of the East, buried for now under an 0-3 start that the margin fully earned.

report.headline: Beaten by the margin, not luck, but 42% opponent shooting won't last
report.take:
Miami opens 2026-27 at 0-3 and last on the site's Teams tab, 30th of 30, with a Net Rtg of -15.2 that ranks 29th. There is no hard-luck story to tell yet. W vs Pt Diff sits at 0, and the margin implies zero wins. The Heat haven't been losing coin flips. They've been outplayed at both ends, against Minnesota, Detroit and Charlotte. This comes off a 43-39 year with a Net Rtg of 2.2 and a 12th-place site rank. The frontcourt now runs through Giannis Antetokounmpo, 14th of 77 on his tab and the clear focal point of the roster.

The offense is the more structural problem. Its ORtg of 105.5 ranks 27th. The Heat are taking 44.2% of their shots from three, 10th in volume, and hitting only 30.3%, so the volume bet is losing badly. The wings carry a D- grade for a reason. Andrew Wiggins is at a 40.4 TS % and Klay Thompson at 51.0, and Tim Hardaway Jr. off the bench is at 34.7. Antetokounmpo (36.8 USG %, 61.4 TS %) and Davion Mitchell (64.7 TS %) are doing their part, and almost no one around them is. At the other end, the DRtg of 120.7 (24th) hides an odd shape. Opponents are barely getting to the rim (Opp Rim Rate 19.7, 3rd) and are converting poorly there (61.1%, 7th). They are killing Miami from outside instead, at 42% from three, worst in the league and 8 points above the league mean. Shooting guards in particular have feasted for 38 points a game.

This is a three-game sample, and the noisiest numbers are the loudest ones. Opponents' three-point percentage swings more than almost anything else on defense. A paint-first scheme concedes threes by design, but not at 42%. This franchise has finished top-10 in Def Rank in most recent seasons, so a 24th-ranked defense is unlikely to hold. The on-off figures are pure sample noise and say nothing yet. Antetokounmpo sits at -36.2 and Bobby Portis at +39.8. Two things look more worrying because they don't depend on opponents' luck. One is the rebounding: REB % is 44.3, 29th, after 49.9 last season. The other is a wing group with no reliable shooter.

The losses are getting closer: 106-131, then 111-128, then 110-115. Expect the defensive numbers to drift back toward the middle as opponents cool off, which should turn this into a roughly .500-caliber team. The ceiling is capped by the wings and the glass until one of those changes. The coming week won't make the climb easy.

strengths.title: A wall around the paint
strengths.body: Opponents take only 19.7% of their shots at the rim, 3rd-fewest in the league and far below the league mean, and they finish just 61.1% there. That comes from scheme and size, with Adebayo and Antetokounmpo walling off the lane. It is the part of this defense most likely to last. The ugly DRtg is coming from outside, not inside.

strengths.title: Giannis is carrying the offense
strengths.body: Antetokounmpo is using 36.8% of possessions while on the floor at a 61.4 TS %, with 85 points in three games. He rates 14th of 77 at his position, by far the best-ranked regular on the roster. That production is real and repeatable. The problem is how little the rest of the rotation adds to it.

strengths.title: They don't give it away
strengths.body: A TOV % of 12.7 ranks 8th, below the league average, in line with the low-turnover habits of recent Heat seasons. Mitchell's 26 assists against a modest usage show a steady hand at the point. Ball security is a floor that keeps games like the Charlotte loss close.

concerns.title: The wings can't shoot
concerns.body: The wing group grades D-. Wiggins is at a 40.4 TS % and Thompson at 51.0, and the team hits only 30.3% from three while taking a top-10 share of its shots from there. Some of the cold shooting will warm up. Still, a group this weak around a high-usage star means defenses can load up on Antetokounmpo. That is a roster problem more than a slump.

concerns.title: Losing the glass at both ends
concerns.body: REB % has fallen to 44.3, 29th, from 49.9 last season. ORB % is 21.1, 27th, and RPG is well below the league. Rebounding settles faster than shooting, so this is the number to worry about if it doesn't move within a couple of weeks. A rim-protecting defense gives back its gains when it can't finish possessions.

concerns.title: Shooters are teeing off
concerns.body: Opponents are shooting 42% from three, last in the league and 8 points over the league mean. Shooting guards are scoring 38 a game, the worst mark relative to their own averages. Part of this is the price of packing the paint, and part of it is noise that should fade. The perimeter closeouts still need to be better than this.

trend.note: Three straight losses, but each closer than the last: 106-131 to Minnesota, 111-128 to Detroit, then 110-115 at Charlotte. It's a tiny sample, but the direction is right.

weekAhead.headline: Dallas is the opening; Atlanta and the Lakers test everything
weekAhead.body:
Four games, two at home and two away. Only one opponent sits below Miami's level on paper. Dallas comes to Miami first at 1-2 and 23rd on the site, and it is the clearest chance to get off the schedule's floor. The Mavericks turn it over at a 16.9 TOV % (27th), have a D frontcourt, and allow 34.67 points a game to power forwards. That is an invitation for Antetokounmpo.

It gets harder from there. Atlanta (2-1, 7th on the site, Net Rtg 15.4) launches 46.3% of its shots from three, exactly the attack that has burned Miami's defense. Indiana comes in with the 2nd-best eFG % in the league. The week closes at the Lakers, who own the league's best ORtg at 126.5. One win is the realistic baseline, and two would count as real progress.

keyMatchups.title: Giannis against soft power-forward defense
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows 34.67 points a game to power forwards, and Atlanta's power-forward defense ranks last relative to opponents' averages. The Hawks also allow 76.7% at the rim, 29th. Miami's best player gets two of the friendliest possible matchups for his game. If he can't break those defenses open, the week goes 0-4 territory.

keyMatchups.title: The three-point defense against volume shooters
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's 3PA Rate of 46.3 ranks 4th, and Indiana shoots a 58.4 eFG %. Miami's paint-first defense concedes threes by design. Against these two teams, the Heat find out whether 42% opponent shooting was bad luck or bad closeouts.

keyMatchups.title: A glass the Lakers leave open
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers' ORtg is 126.5, first in the league, but they rank last in RPG at 37 and 28th in DRB %. Indiana is 29th in ORB %. That makes this a week where Miami's rebounding slump can be tested against weak glass teams rather than punished by strong ones.

weekAhead.watch: Whether opponents' 3-point percentage starts falling from 42% while Miami keeps them away from the rim. That is the difference between a bad start and a bad defense.

restOfSeason.body:
With 79 games left, the 0-3 start barely moves the long-run picture. The current numbers carried over a full season look absurd because they are built on three games. Expect the defense to drift back toward the middle of the league as opponents' three-point shooting cools. The rim protection underneath it looks genuine, and this franchise's defense has rarely ranked this low. The offense should also warm up from 30.3% on threes, if not by much.

What doesn't regress on its own is the roster shape: a D- wing group, a D backcourt, and rebounding that has fallen from about even last season to 29th. That points to a team around last year's level rather than a leap: something like 36 to 45 wins, a Net Rtg near zero, and a fight for play-in position in the East. Upside depends on finding a wing who can make shots next to Antetokounmpo.
swingFactors: Rebounding returning toward last season's level

confidence.note: Three games; shooting-driven numbers are at their noisiest.
